title: Custom Memory Slab/Arena Allocator without Profiling
pattern: Re-implementing a custom slab, pool, or arena memory allocator inside application code before measuring standard memory allocation overhead.
why_bad: Modern system allocators (like jemalloc) are heavily optimized for multi-threaded thread caching and prevent fragmentation. Custom allocators often introduce memory safety issues, memory leaks, high overhead, and can easily run slower than standard malloc/free [317, 328, 422].
detection: Custom memory block allocations, unsafe pointer recycling, or manual reuse of discarded nodes in vector pools instead of normal drop and instantiations.
counterexample: High-speed compiler implementations where a massive pool of AST nodes is allocated and dropped entirely as a single arena at compilation end. `Context-dependent`.
fix: Use the default standard allocator or configure the program to use jemalloc globally.
source: *A Philosophy of Software Design*, Chapter 20 (p. 317); *Code Complete*, Section 25.2 (p. 328); *Release It!*, Section 10 (p. 422).
